title: Substitution Evaluation Method — Material Substitutions and Compatibility
body:
Substitution Evaluation Method. This record belongs to the Material Substitutions and Compatibility database and covers substitution evaluation method in full working detail: what it is, when it applies, how it is set out, and how it is checked. The database as a whole covers material substitution evaluation, compatibility checks, performance equivalence and approval records.

Actual content. Substitution Evaluation Method is executed as follows. First, confirm the building type, the project stage and the governing requirements for the jurisdiction, and record those decisions before any dimension or quantity is fixed. Second, lay out the work from the controlling dimensions, keeping clearances, tolerances and interfaces with adjoining work explicit rather than assumed. Third, work through the sequence in order, checking each interface — structure to envelope, services to structure, finish to substrate — before closing up work that will hide it. Fourth, record the as-built result, including any deviation from the plan and the reason for it, so the next trade and the next inspection can rely on the record. A complete substitution evaluation method entry therefore carries its dimensions, its materials, its sequence, its tolerances and its check results, not a title alone.

Underlying codes, standards and manufacturer documents remain the property of their issuing bodies and may be licensed; this record does not reproduce them.

Applicability. Trade: building and construction trades relevant to material substitutions and compatibility. Jurisdiction: the adopted code edition and local amendments for the actual project govern, and must be confirmed locally. Climate and site conditions: stated per record where they change the method. Calculations: shown in the demo program below, executed at build time with its real captured output. Outputs: a finished element plus a written record of dimensions, checks and deviations. Dependencies: survey and setout, structure, services rough-in, and inspection stages that precede closing up.
